articles.title: Global shares are trading mixed as market optimism about AI gets tempered by Iran worries
articles.description: Global shares are trading mixed amid investor interest in technology-related issues and ongoing worries about the war in Iran. Benchmarks declined in early Thursday trading in France, Germany and Britain. In Asia, shares finished higher in Tokyo and Seoul, while falling in Sydney. In Tokyo trading, issues expected to get a boost from the solid demand in computer chips and AI-related growth finished higher, including Advantest Corp., Tokyo Electron and SoftBank Group Corp. Hong Kong and Shanghai markets were closed for a holiday. Oil prices rose. Dow futures fell, while S&P 500 futures were little changed.

articles.title: Global Market: European shares slide as surging bond yields hit risk appetite
articles.description: European shares opened the final quarter lower as elevated global bond yields and persistent inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment. The STOXX 600 fell 1%, with banks among the biggest decliners. Higher energy costs and expectations of prolonged interest rates pressured equities, while softer oil prices offered limited relief to markets.

articles.description: Oil prices bounced back above $100 a barrel on Thursday as a US-Iran deal remained elusive, while European stocks fell and US government bonds came off their worst quarter since 1994, with the 10-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2007.

articles.title: FOREX-Euro slides to 17-month low, hit by rates and inflation cocktail
articles.description: As political instabilities linger, the euro has descended to its lowest point in over 17 months when measured against the dollar. This shift has prompted investors to favor the dollar, which is showing strength across various currencies. Meanwhile, the Australian dollar has reached a two-month low due to disappointing local inflation forecasts. European markets, burdened by surging oil prices and escalating inflation, are facing a formidable set of economic hurdles.

articles.title: Why Indian stocks are falling: CA Sarthak Ahuja explains US bond yield impact on markets
articles.description: Indian equities have faced renewed pressure as rising US Treasury yields, elevated crude oil prices and foreign investor selling weigh on market sentiment. CA Sarthak Ahuja has highlighted how higher US bond yields could influence global capital flows and the relative attractiveness of Indian equities.
